plain.li: [takeback,warm] We talked it over at the long table, the way you taught us, and the answer is yes. Come home.
[takeback,warm,theirLowtech] The fire was yours before it was ours. Come and sit at it again.
[takeback,warm,theirHightech] Approved by everyone who voted. The place is yours again whenever you are ready.
[takeback,cordial] We have thought about it, and we agree. The place was yours first, and it can be yours again.
[takeback,cordial,call] Yes. Come and take it over; we will open the gates.
[takeback,cordial,theirLowtech] The elders say it is right. What was handed on can be handed back.
[takeback,cool] Very well. It has been hard going on our own, and we will not pretend otherwise.
[takeback,cool,theirHightech] Agreed. Running the place alone costs more than we have.
[takeback,refusal] No. You handed it to us, and we have made it ours.
[takeback,refusal,theirLowtech] A gift given is not taken back. The fire stays with us.
[takeback,refusal,theirHightech] Declined. The town runs itself now, and its people want it that way.
[takeback,refusal,call] I'm sorry, but no. People here are proud of what they've built.
[former] We still hold our meetings at the long table in the evening, the way we did when this was {OLDCOLONY}.
[former] Some days I still catch myself thinking of {TOWN} as {OLDCOLONY}, and of all of you as down the hall.
[former] The rooms here still go by the names they had in the colony's days, and nobody has thought to change them.
[former,years] It has been {YEARSSINCE} since we stood together and handed {OLDCOLONY} over. It does not feel that long.
[former,tribal] We keep the old fire as you kept it, and the young ones ask for the stories of when we were all one band.
[former,medieval] The charter you left us hangs in the hall, and we read it out on the day it was given.
[former,industrial] The town charter is framed by the door of the meeting room, and nobody has let the dust settle on it.
[former,spacer] The administration runs on the old colony's systems still, patched where they wore through.
[new] The older ones here talk about {OLDCOLONY} as if it were yesterday. I hope we do it credit.
[new,years] It is {YEARSSINCE} since {OLDCOLONY} became {TOWN}, and the people here still speak of you as kin of the place.
[struggling] I will not pretend it is easy here. Times are hard, and some nights the hall is very quiet.
[struggling] We are getting by, just, and I think of the colony's stores more often than I would like to admit.
[poor] It has been a lean season, but nobody has gone hungry yet.
[steady] Things are steady here. The fields are in, the roofs hold, and the quarrels are small ones.
[thriving] {TOWN} is doing well. There are new faces at the table, and we have had to build on.
[flourishing] I never thought I would write this, but {TOWN} is doing better than {OLDCOLONY} ever did. You would hardly know the place.
[asks] {ASKER} asks after {KIN} every time a letter goes out, so: how is {KIN}?
[asks] {ASKER} sends {KIN} their love, and wants to hear how {KIN} is getting on.
[asks,former] {ASKER} made me promise to write that {KIN} is missed here, more than {KIN} knows.
Write when you can. Letters from {COLONY} are read out at supper, every word of them.
If your caravans come this way, the gates of {TOWN} are open to them.
[welcome] You came home.
[welcome] I hoped you would come back.
[welcome] There is a place at the table for you.
[welcome] Look at you, back where you belong.
[welcome] I kept asking every traveler about you.
[welcome] Welcome home, it has not been the same without you.
[back] I missed this place more than I knew.
[back] It is good to be home.
[back] I kept thinking about you all, every day.
[back] The road back felt shorter than the road away.
[back] They send their love from the town.
[back] I am staying this time.
